Observed exactly those. After POST /sales/:refund/returned-items for the jeans: 41 = 700, 42 = 2,000, line 4 = 2,000, line 29 = $1,021.17, line 36 still 0: as hand-computed. priceMileage on 100 mi 2025-12-30, 40 mi 2026-03-10, 25.5 mi 2026-08-01: 7000 + 2900 + 1938 = 11,838 cents, observed 11,838; the rate table matches irs.gov/tax-professionals/standard-mileage-rates fetched today (2025 70c IR-2024-312; 2026 Jan-Jun 72.5c IR-2025-128; Jul-Dec 76c IR-2026-29). reconcile1099k with box 1a $1,570.00 against books items 1,500 / +shipping 1,570 / +tax 1,690: closest items_shipping, difference 0, tolerance max($1, 0.5%) = $7.85: as observed. evidence.completeness: The 2026-11-26 feature list re-run plus what was added since: multi-unit linking (units.ts), unlinked-units warning on the worksheet (schedule-c.ts:289-297, unlinked-sales.test.ts), per-trip IRS mileage (mileage-rates.ts), 1099-K reconciliation route and pure module (reports.ts:417, reconcile-1099k.ts), returned items back to stock (sales.ts:433). Score 2 is before this PR; its new worker test (four items added out of date order, one written off) catches both survivors.
evidence.craft: Read store.ts (255 lines), units.ts, the Part III loop of schedule-c.ts (360-392), mileage-rates.ts, reconcile-1099k.ts head, ebay.ts. The matching rule is now one pure function shared by both paths (units.ts) instead of two diverging copies; the 1099-K module states what it cannot know (whether a platform's box 1a includes tax) instead of guessing. Remaining nit: ebay.ts stored eBay's '--' empty cell as an order id on charge rows (fixed here).
evidence.claims: ARCHITECTURE.md:78 now says 'one item per unit' (backed by units.ts); the mileage table's sources match irs.gov; FORM_1099K_GROSS quote 'without regard to any adjustments for credits' is the i1099k wording; DEPLOY.md and VENTURE.yaml state not deployed and paid plans dark. The worksheet disclaimer ('Worksheet only ... not a tax return and not tax advice') is in schedule-c.ts:206.
evidence.fitness: A reseller's year (eBay report, bought items, one return, trips) walks through to a Schedule C worksheet a preparer can check line by line, with a 1099-K tie-out. No seller can do it yet: the app is not deployed (DEPLOY.md, 'Not yet').
evidence.domain: Against the 2025 Schedule C instructions and IRS standard-mileage notices: line 1/2 placement, fee credits on line 10, Part III specific identification with returns re-entering closing inventory at cost (not as a purchase on line 36), and per-date mileage rates all follow practice. Matching takes oldest first among items held on the sale date, a reasonable default for identical SKUs.

verdict: Does not meet the bar yet, on verification alone (correctness 3, claims 3, verification 2; median 3); finished (completeness 3). Both high defects of 2026-11-26 are closed: a quantity-2 order now costs both units and a sale can no longer take an item bought after it. Five more of the nine earlier defects are closed (unlinked-units warning, per-date IRS mileage, 1099-K tie-out, returns back to stock, the architecture note). Every output recomputed by hand matched to the cent: Schedule C Part I and Part III from the eBay fixture, Part III after a return, line 9 over three IRS rate periods (table checked against irs.gov today), and the 1099-K bases. Verification stays at 2 because the two mutants that survived last time still survived on arrival; this PR adds the worker test that catches both and fixes the eBay '--' order id, so a later re-audit can score it again. Fitness is 2 because the app is not deployed.
